title: Choose the lesson panel layout
question: Three layouts for the lesson monitor, all in the Connections app's own look (white title band with the green and yellow stripe, grey ground, white cards, Calibri). The Gen 4 display now has its own monitor with a yellow ring overlay, so these show the lesson and the armrest only. Pick one, steer it, or ask for another hand.

options.label: One action, big armrest
options.lineage: Instruction band over one large armrest stage
options.thesis: One action across the top, and below it the armrest at full size with the manual's photo of every button to press, in order.
materials: manual line drawing of the handle with ringed buttons
options.viewport: Full-width band with the one action and why; below, the handle drawing large on the left and the numbered manual photos on the right; a step rail along the bottom. The display's own monitor gets a yellow ring overlay.
options.risk: Steps done only on the display leave the big armrest stage with little to say.

raised.raise: The band carries exactly one action at monumental size; the next step waits dimmed beside it, never more.
The step rail punches each finished step; only the current leg wears the yellow.

options.label: Manual procedure page
options.thesis: The lesson reads like the manual's own numbered procedure, with the manual's photo beside every step and the current step opened up.
options.viewport: Left: the whole lesson as numbered steps, finished ones collapsed with a check, the current one expanded with why, hint and the button photos. Right: the handle drawing at full height, with a line saying what to watch on the display monitor.
options.risk: With seven or more steps the list competes with the live views for attention.

options.label: Trainee above, machine below
options.lineage: Next action on top, what the machine saw underneath
options.thesis: The top of the screen is for the trainee, the strip underneath shows the instructor what the machine actually saw, press by press.
materials: large handle drawing with the target
live event strip: presses, lights, game changes
options.viewport: Top two thirds: the action and the manual photos on the left, the handle drawing with the targets on the right. Bottom third: a timeline of presses, cloud lights and mistakes with time on step.
options.risk: A trainee may read the log instead of the instruction.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: a mistake stays in the strip, struck through, never erased.

options.label: Airport wayfinding
options.thesis: Only the next decision, at monumental size.
options.viewport: One yellow band with the next action and its pictogram.
options.risk: Yellow bands would fight the app's own yellow action button.
options.case: Fuses partly: trainees know signage, but a band-only screen hides where the button is.
options.kept: One action per band at monumental size.

options.label: Orienteering course
options.thesis: Travel control to control, the active leg in one colour.
options.viewport: A course line across the steps with punched controls.
options.risk: Map metaphor means nothing to most operators.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the map is not the machine.
options.kept: Finished controls get punched; only the active leg is coloured.

options.label: Ticket wallet
options.thesis: Each leg tears off; states stamp themselves.
options.viewport: Steps as coupons torn off in sequence.
options.risk: Costume of paper on a working screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coupons add ceremony, not clarity.

options.label: Centre-rail edition
options.thesis: Two columns around a rail of keys.
options.viewport: Twinned text columns with a key rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dense reading does not fit hands-on training.
options.kept: States drawn as marks, not colour alone.

options.label: Grid specimen
options.viewport: Monumental grid letters over small text.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in training is built cell by cell.
options.kept: Everything snaps to one visible grid.

options.label: Variable type specimen
options.lineage: Axis sliders over a glyph grid
options.viewport: One letter fills the screen, sliders below.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no axis in a lesson to drag.
options.kept: A live readout that answers every input at once.
